subject: health
essentialQuestion: How do I find information I can trust and use it to make a healthy choice?

prompts.prompt: Explain trusted adults and health helpers in your own words and give or identify a valid example.

Use a diagram of a general figure or character rather than your own body, a picture sequence, a model, a described demonstration, or a checked source, to show what you learned about medicine and household product safety.
Apply what you learned about reliable information and advertising to a new fictional situation. Show the steps or name the source you relied on.
A made-up character makes an unsafe or unreliable choice involving saying no and getting away. Explain what is wrong, correct it, and say why the correction is safer.
Connect trusted adults and health helpers with caring for our shared community. Explain how the two ideas support or depend on one another.
Present the strongest evidence from the unit task: Create a short health advocacy message for family or community, supported by one adult-checked reliable source.
Name one skill you can now use somewhere else, one way to check your own work, and one question you still have. This is about the skill, not about your private life; nothing private has to be shared.
